applicable_when: The kernel uses XBLOCK=128 for xnumel=4 — 128 threads compete for only 4 real X-dimension elements, causing massive waste and uncoalesced sector utilization (only 16/32 bytes used per sector). The grid is (1, 4096) producing a partial wave that accounts for up to 50% of runtime. Reshaping to XBLOCK=4 and YBLOCK=32 aligns the tile to the actual data dimensions, enables coalesced Y-dimension loads, and eliminates the partial wave. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the load pointer tells the compiler the access is contiguous and aligned, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads instead of scalar 32-bit loads.
